compute.basis: No code released; the dual-GNN (two residual GraphSAGE models trained alternately via rollout-based ranking losses), multilevel coarsening, local-state enumeration, coarse conflict-graph MIS via PySCIPOpt, and completion pipeline must all be reimplemented from the text, then trained on 800 graphs and evaluated on 50 n=500 graphs; inference itself is CPU-feasible (paper used a 6GB laptop GPU) but reimplementation and training dominate.

blockers: No code or configs released (empty code_links)
Training requires rollout-based supervision over the full coarsening+solve pipeline, which is expensive to reimplement and run
Exact baseline (643 s/graph) and ReduMIS comparison require external solvers (PySCIPOpt, ReduMIS binary)
Reproducing the exact 19.20 mean requires matching unspecified training details (rollout counts, loss weighting, seeds)
title: Dual-GNN Multilevel Coarsening for Maximum Independent Set
